summary: An Earth.Org article by Rose Morrison (July 2023) asks whether humanity will ever be able to go without fossil fuels, and concludes that alternatives are increasingly available but still face cost, environmental and access obstacles. It surveys alternative fuels for vehicles, aviation and fuels in development, then discusses electricity growth, the challenges of cost, environmental impact and access, and the reasons for phasing out fossil fuels, including health, ecosystems and the economy. It closes by noting that fossil fuel reserves are finite and that continued work on renewable energy could eventually power the world largely without fossil fuels.
one_line: Earth.Org article surveying alternative fuels, electrification, and the cost and access barriers to phasing out fossil fuels.
key_facts: Fossil fuels make up 81% of the Earth's energy supply, according to the article.
Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is produced from non-petroleum feedstocks such as woody biomass, fats, oils, and municipal solid waste.
The aviation industry's efforts aim to go net zero by 2050, with SAF supporting that goal.
According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), energy use in the country has steadily increased by 4 trillion kilowatt hours since 1950.
The UN's Global Electric Mobility Programme focuses on increasing the use of electric vehicles in 50 low and middle-income countries.
Producing hydrogen by pulling the element from the air is currently more than $200 per ton.
The International Nuclear Engineering Project originally estimated the cost of introducing nuclear fusion at around US$6.5 billion, but newer estimates put the price nearer $24 billion.
The World Health Organization (WHO) predicts an additional 250,000 deaths between 2030 and 2050 from malnutrition, malaria, diarrhoea, and heat stress.
The scientific community expects global temperatures to increase by about 2C by 2050.
According to the World Economic Forum (WEF), climate change could wipe out 18% of global gross domestic product (GDP) by 2050.
According to research from Stanford University's Millennium Alliance for Humanity and the Biosphere, the Earth has only 30 years of oil, 40 years of gas, and 70 years of coal left.
Trillions of dollars are directed to subsidising fossil fuels each year, while most funds are still directed to petroleum.
Electric vehicles produce zero tailpipe emissions, and a growing number of charging stations worldwide is reducing the need for hybrid vehicles.
Geo-engineering manipulates the atmosphere to reduce carbon and reflect back solar radiation, but many scientists believe it would not reduce the number of emissions entering the atmosphere.
Dimethyl Ether is a synthetic alternative to diesel that can eliminate particulate emissions in semi-trucks.
